name: X-linked adrenal hypoplasia congenita (NR0B1/DAX1)
aliases: adrenal hypoplasia congenita with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: An X-linked disorder of adrenal development caused by mutations in NR0B1, which encodes the nuclear receptor DAX1
Typically affects males and presents with primary adrenal insufficiency, often with a salt-wasting crisis in infancy or later childhood
Presentation includes hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia and hyperpigmentation from combined glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism characteristically emerges later and manifests as absent or arrested puberty
The combination of primary adrenal failure and later gonadotropin deficiency is a strong diagnostic clue
Contiguous gene deletions at the locus can co-occur with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and glycerol kinase deficiency
Impaired spermatogenesis frequently persists, so fertility is often affected despite hormone replacement
reference.pathophysiology: DAX1, the product of NR0B1, is a nuclear receptor essential for the development and function of the adrenal cortex and for the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. Loss-of-function mutations lead to failure of normal adrenocortical development, producing primary adrenal insufficiency with deficiency of both glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids. The same gene is required for normal gonadotropin regulation and gonadal function, so affected males also develop hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, typically becoming apparent around the age of expected puberty. The X-linked inheritance explains the predominance of affected males.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism such as Kallmann syndrome
additionalInvestigations: Serum electrolytes, glucose and paired cortisol with ACTH
Plasma renin and aldosterone to assess mineralocorticoid status
ACTH stimulation testing to confirm adrenal insufficiency
Gonadotropins and sex steroids, especially around the age of expected puberty
Molecular genetic testing of NR0B1 including assessment for contiguous gene deletions
redFlags: Adrenal (salt-wasting) crisis with hypotension, hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia requiring emergency treatment
Hypoglycaemia and collapse in an infant or child from glucocorticoid deficiency
Absent or arrested puberty indicating evolving hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Associated neuromuscular features suggesting a contiguous gene deletion syndrome
reference.prognosis: With lifelong glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement and induction of puberty when required, survival and development are generally good, although impaired fertility commonly persists and adrenal crises remain a lifelong risk if replacement lapses.
pitfalls: Misattributing the adrenal insufficiency to congenital adrenal hyperplasia and missing the underlying diagnosis
Failing to anticipate later hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and delayed puberty
Overlooking associated neuromuscular disease from a contiguous gene deletion
Underestimating the ongoing risk of adrenal crisis during intercurrent illness
management: Lifelong glucocorticoid replacement with hydrocortisone and mineralocorticoid replacement with fludrocortisone for the combined adrenal insufficiency
Salt supplementation in infancy to support mineralocorticoid deficiency

Emergency management of adrenal crisis with intravenous fluids, parenteral hydrocortisone and correction of hypoglycaemia and electrolyte disturbance, supported by sick-day dosing rules and a steroid emergency card
Induction of puberty and testosterone replacement for the hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, with assisted reproduction or gonadotropin therapy for the commonly impaired fertility
Regular monitoring of growth, electrolytes, blood pressure and pubertal progression

Molecular testing of NR0B1 including assessment for a contiguous gene deletion involving Duchenne muscular dystrophy and glycerol kinase deficiency, with genetic counselling for this X-linked condition
Endocrinology-led multidisciplinary follow-up with escalation for suspected crisis
